- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to account for reversal.  
- Model consistently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), leading to overshoot; apply dampening factor of 0.85–0.90 to peak forecasts.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion within 5–7 days after a spike, model fails to correct; add a 1–3 day lagged mean reversion term to forecast.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture short-term sentiment-driven volatility; weight sentiment history more heavily in early days of forecast window.  
- When sentiment shifts from positive to negative within 3 days, model often misses the reversal; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% if sentiment drops below 0.33.
